questions.title: Finding an Unknown Probability from Total Probability Axiom

parts.text: A discrete random variable $X$ takes values 1, 2, and 3. The probabilities are given by $P(X = 1) = \frac{1}{6}$ and $P(X = 2) = \frac{1}{3}$. Given that $\sum P(X = x) = 1$, find the value of $P(X = 3)$.

questions.title: Determining Constant k in a Linear Probability Formula

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ has probability function $P(X = x) = kx$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$, where $k$ is a constant. Find the value of $k$ and hence find $P(X = 3)$.

questions.title: Linear Transformation of a Fair Spinner Score

parts.text: A fair 4-sided spinner has faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4. Let $S$ be the number shown when the spinner is spun once. The random variable $Y$ is defined by $Y = 3S - 2$. List the possible values of $Y$ and find $P(Y \ge 4)$.
A bag contains 3 red counters and 2 blue counters. Two counters are chosen at random without replacement. Let $X$ be the number of red counters chosen. Find $P(X = 1)$.

questions.title: Number of Heads in Two Coin Flips

parts.text: Two fair coins are tossed. Let $X$ be the number of heads obtained. Find $P(X \le 1)$.

questions.title: Maximum Score of Two Fair 4-Sided Spinners

parts.text: Two fair 4-sided spinners, each numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are spun simultaneously. Let $M$ be the larger of the two numbers spun, or the common number if they are equal. Find $P(M = 3)$.

questions.title: Drawing Counters Without Replacement and Inequality Probabilities

parts.text: A bag contains 4 white counters and 2 black counters. Two counters are chosen at random without replacement. Let $X$ be the number of black counters chosen. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Find the probability that at least 1 black counter is chosen.

questions.title: Distribution with Decreasing Linear Probability Formula

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities given by $P(X = x) = c(5 - x)$, where $c$ is a constant. Show that $c = \frac{1}{10}$.
Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$, and hence find $P(1 < X \le 3)$.

questions.title: Transformed Discrete Variable from a Symmetrical Spinner

parts.text: A fair 4-sided spinner has faces numbered $-1, 0, 1, 2$. Let $S$ be the face shown when the spinner is spun once. The random variable $Y$ is defined by $Y = S^2 - 1$. State all possible values of $Y$ and show that $P(Y = 0) = \frac{1}{2}$.
Draw up the probability distribution table for $Y$, and hence find $P(Y > -1)$.

questions.title: Difference of Two Fair Spinners with Unequal Face Sets

parts.text: A fair spinner $A$ has sides numbered 1, 2, 3. A fair spinner $B$ has sides numbered 0, 2. The two spinners are spun once simultaneously. Let $X$ be the score on spinner $A$ minus the score on spinner $B$. List all possible pairs of scores $(A, B)$ and draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Find the probability that $X > 0$, and find the probability that $X$ is an even number.

questions.title: Stopping Game Model with Independent Trials and Conditional Probability

parts.text: An archer shoots at a target up to a maximum of 3 times. On any single shot, the probability of hitting the target is 0.4 independently. The activity stops immediately if the archer hits the target, or after 3 shots if no hit has occurred. Let $X$ be the total number of shots taken. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Given that the archer takes more than 1 shot, find the conditional probability that the archer takes exactly 2 shots.

A box contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. Three balls are selected at random without replacement. Let $X$ be the number of red balls selected. State all possible values of $X$ and explain why $X$ cannot take the value 4.
Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$, giving each probability as an exact fraction in simplest form.
Given that at least 1 red ball is selected, find the conditional probability that at least 2 red balls are selected.

questions.title: Distribution of Maximum from Independent Spinners and Cumulative Formulation

parts.text: Two fair 4-sided spinners, each numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are spun simultaneously. Let $X$ be the larger of the two numbers shown, or the common number if both spinners show the same number. Using the cumulative probability relationship $P(X \le x) = \left(\frac{x}{4}\right)^2$ or otherwise, show that $P(X = 2) = \frac{3}{16}$, and find $P(X = 1)$.
Complete the probability distribution table for $X$.
Given that $X \ge 2$, find the conditional probability that $X$ is an odd number.
